PART I. Lemma (C1A) (Simon Ch. 2, 1.5, on balls). Let f: R^n -> R be Lipschitz, m real and eps > 0. Then there is g in C^1(R^n) with L^n(B_m(0) meet {f != g}) < eps.
Proof. Let K be a Lipschitz constant of f. Put B := B_m(0), which is compact, so L^n(B) < infinity. If m < 0 then B is empty and g := 0 works, so assume m >= 0. Let D := {x : f is differentiable at x} and Df(x) := fderiv R f x.
I.1 Rademacher.
- By (Rad) and (Mea), D is Borel, L^n(R^n minus D) = 0, and x -> Df(x) is Borel.
- For x in D and v in R^n, |Df(x)v| = lim_{t -> 0+} |f(x + t v) - f(x)|/t <= K|v|. So ||Df(x)|| <= K.
I.2 Lusin.
- Let nu := L^n restricted to B, a finite Borel measure. By (Reg) it satisfies the hypothesis of (Lus).
- Let e_1, ..., e_n be the standard basis. Apply (Lus) to nu, the Borel set B meet D, and each of the n + 1 Borel functions u_0 := 0 and u_i(x) := Df(x)e_i (1 <= i <= n), with eta := eps/(4(n + 1)).
- This gives closed sets C_0, ..., C_n contained in B meet D with nu((B meet D) minus C_i) < eps/(4(n + 1)) and u_i continuous on C_i.

I.3 Remainder quotients (the book's R and eta_k).
- For x, y in C with x != y put R(x, y) := (f(y) - f(x) - Df(x)(y - x))/|y - x|. Then |R(x, y)| <= K + ||Df(x)|| <= 2K.

- Then 0 <= eta_{k+1} <= eta_k <= 2K.
I.4 Pointwise convergence. Let x in C, so x is in D, and let eps' > 0. Since f is differentiable at x with derivative Df(x), there is r > 0 with |f(y) - f(x) - Df(x)(y - x)| <= eps'|y - x| whenever |y - x| < r. Hence eta_k(x) <= eps' as soon as 1/k <= r. So eta_k(x) -> 0 for every x in C.
I.5 Measurability.
- Fix k. For y in C let O_y := {x in C : 0 < |y - x| < 1/k}, a relatively open subset of C. Define psi_y on C by psi_y(x) := |R(x, y)| for x in O_y and psi_y(x) := 0 otherwise.

- On C, eta_k is the pointwise supremum of the psi_y (y in C). So each set {x in C : eta_k(x) > a} is a union of relatively open sets, hence relatively open in C.
- C is closed, so these sets are Borel in R^n. Since eta_k = 0 off C, eta_k is a Borel function on R^n.

(a) f is Lipschitz, hence continuous on A.
(b) D is continuous on A, because A is contained in C (I.2).
(c) Let K' contained in A be compact and eps' > 0. By uniform convergence on A (contained in A_0), choose k with eta_k(x) <= eps' for all x in A, and put delta' := 1/k. Let x in K' and y in A with |x - y| < delta'. If y = x, both sides of the required inequality are 0. PART II. Proof of Lemma T. Fix n >= 1, U open and V.

(b) For every compact K contained in U, mu(K) = int_{M meet K} theta dH^n < infinity (structure field integrableOn_mult).

II.2 C^1 cover (Lemma 1.2; the book's appeal to Ch. 2, 1.5 is Lemma C1A of Part I).

Let G_{jmi}: R^n -> E have the coordinates g^c. Then G_{jmi} is C^1, and since {F_j != G_{jmi}} lies in U_c {F_j^c != g^c}, L^n(B_m(0) meet {F_j != G_{jmi}}) < 1/i.
(c) Let Z_j := U_m n_{i>=1} (B_m(0) meet {F_j != G_{jmi}}).
- Each inner intersection has L^n-measure <= 1/i for every i, hence 0. So L^n(Z_j) = 0 = H^n(Z_j), and H^n(F_j(Z_j)) <= Lip(F_j)^n H^n(Z_j) = 0 by (Lip).
- If u is not in Z_j, choose m >= |u|. Then u is in B_m(0) but not in the intersection, so F_j(u) = G_{jmi}(u) for some i.
- Hence F_j(R^n) is contained in F_j(Z_j) union U_{m,i} G_{jmi}(R^n).
(d) Critical set. For a C^1 map G: R^n -> E let C_G := {u : DG(u) is not injective}.
- G is differentiable everywhere, so (Crit) gives H^n(G(C_G)) = 0.
- C_G is closed: u -> DG(u) is continuous, and the injective linear maps R^n -> E form an open set (Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.isOpen_injective).
(e) Regular points. Let u not be in C_G, and put c_u := min_{|w|=1} |DG(u) w| > 0 (n >= 1).
- Choose r_u > 0 with ||DG(v) - DG(u)|| <= c_u/2 for |v - u| <= r_u.
- For v, v' in the convex ball B_{r_u}(u), the mean value inequality for v -> G(v) - DG(u) v gives |G(v) - G(v') - DG(u)(v - v')| <= (c_u/2)|v - v'|. Hence |G(v) - G(v')| >= (c_u/2)|v - v'|.

(f) Countable choice.
- Let W_G be the set of open balls W with rational center and positive rational radius (so W is nonempty) such that cl W lies in B°_{r_u}(u) for some u not in C_G. W_G is countable and covers R^n minus C_G.

(g) Enumeration.
- Enumerate the countable set of pairs (G_{jmi}, W) with W in W_{G_{jmi}} as (G_p, W_p), p >= 1. If there are only finitely many, let the remaining W_p be empty. For such p, N_p is empty, every set indexed by p below is empty, all statements about p hold vacuously, and we put c_p := L_p := 1.
- Put N_p := G_p(W_p) and N_0 := M_0 union U_j F_j(Z_j) union U_{j,m,i} G_{jmi}(C_{G_{jmi}}), so H^n(N_0) = 0.
- By (a), (c), (d) and (f), M is contained in N_0 union U_{p>=1} N_p.
(h) Properties of the pieces. Write c_p := c_{W_p} and L_p := L_{W_p} when W_p is in W_{G_p} (for padded empty W_p see (g)).
